title: Heterogeneous Equilibria Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A closed bottle of water fogs up inside, and a hot kiln turns chalky stone into lime and a gas. Solids, liquids and gases sit in one equilibrium, so which of them go into K? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 6, Equilibrium) Diya covers a tumbler of water in her kitchen and we find out why some substances simply drop out of K.

You will learn what a phase is, then watch a closed jar of water on the molecule bench: evaporation and condensation balance, and the vapour pressure stays the same even when half the water is taken out, so Kp = p(H2O). A chocolate bar shows why a pure solid or liquid has a fixed concentration. We build K for CaCO3(s) = CaO(s) + CO2(g) step by step (Kc = [CO2], Kp = pCO2), sort Ni(CO)4, Ag2O and CO2 + C examples into keep and drop, use NCERT's value at 1100 K (pCO2 = 2.0 x 10^5 Pa, Kp = 2.00), solve NCERT's CO2 + C problem (Kp = 3.0, 0.66 bar CO and 0.15 bar CO2), show the exam trap, then an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 62 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
